source.title: Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders
source.authors: F. Nooralahzadeh; Lea Bogensperger; C. Bluethgen; M. Krauthammer

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures sparse clinical-finding channels in frozen 3D CT image embeddings, not neuron poles or the share of neurons with a single interpretable job. Its results do not test any listed claim version; they are related evidence about a different kind of internal unit.
record.gate_note: The paper reports sparse embedding-coordinate probes and ablations, but embedding coordinates are not identified as neurons. It does not audit neuron explanations on held-out activations, score neuron explanations on new text, estimate interpretable-neuron shares, or test neuron-based attribution graphs. Cited results and report-generation comparisons do not test the claim.
record.test_reason: The study probes the final embedding coordinates of frozen 3D CT encoders (Pillar-0, Merlin). It ranks them by per-finding AUROC and ablates top-10 sets. It does not audit individual neurons' jobs, estimate interpretable-neuron shares, revisit canonical polysemantic neurons, build neuron attribution graphs, or score explanations by held-out simulation. Superposition and network dissection appear only as related-work citations, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that frozen 3D CT encoders store findings in sparse, causally selective coordinate subsets, replicated on Merlin. The probe transfers across hospitals and backbones when anatomy matches and degrades otherwise. They also claim a competitive training-free report-generation pipeline.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes frozen 3D CT vision-encoder embeddings using channel selectivity and mean-difference readouts, rather than auditing neuron poles or testing language-model neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported transfer varies with backbone, anatomy, and institution; the paper says anatomy-mismatched transfer degrades.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pillar-0, top-10 embedding coordinates per finding give mean test AUROC 0.798, versus 0.793 for all 1152 coordinates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clinical findings in frozen 3D CT encoder embeddings are linearly decodable from about 10 coordinates, matching full-embedding performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing a finding's top-10 coordinates drops its own AUROC by 0.0060 on average, versus 0.00003 for other findings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected embedding coordinates are selectively, though weakly, necessary for the corresponding finding's probe score.

fits_no_version.finding: The same coordinates recur across several findings' top-10 sets in Table 5. For example, 897 appears for cardiomegaly, arterial calcification, lymphadenopathy and mosaic attenuation. Related findings show off-diagonal ablation effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual embedding coordinates in CT encoders contribute to several related clinical findings, so the coordinates are not one-to-one with findings.

record.problems: The paper studies embedding coordinates rather than neurons, so its results do not establish neuron-level interpretability or neuron job shares. It notes that rare findings have higher-variance channel estimates and that stability under finer pathology labels, longitudinal follow-up, and multimodal inputs remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted: other reported results concern report generation, classification comparisons, or transfer settings and do not measure neuron-level claims.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper only cites superposition and network dissection and never engages the claim. The units are final pooled embedding coordinates, not neurons; ablation effects are small in absolute terms (0.006 AUROC).
